**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply tokens queued while release waits for the pool lock**

When a streaming refresh is already holding `_lock` to AUTH an idle connection, a concurrent release can run the event while its own token is still unset and then block at the final lock; `re_auth_callback()` subsequently sees this connection in `_in_use_connections` and queues the new token, but this unconditional append exposes it without rerunning `re_auth()`. The next borrower can send a command under stale credentials (the queued token is not applied until that borrower releases it), so the handoff and the in-use-to-available transition need to be made atomic or the token must be reapplied after lock acquisition.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L146-L148](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/2b4eaa6928457c22b9d954dd25ba937032f12ecc/AGENTS.md#L146-L148)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate pool membership before running release side effects**

When `release()` is called with a foreign or already-released connection, membership is not checked until the `remove()` in `finally`, so the new ordering can disconnect a marked foreign connection and dispatch re-auth/custom listeners against it before eventually raising `KeyError`. Previously the remove happened before either side effect, and the sync pool also validates before dispatch; validate or reserve the connection under `_lock` before reconnect handling and listener dispatch to avoid mutating a socket another pool/task may own.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L146-L148](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/2b4eaa6928457c22b9d954dd25ba937032f12ecc/AGENTS.md#L146-L148)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

### Releasing connections miss concurrent token AUTH **Medium Severity** A connection remains in `_in_use_connections` until after deferred `re_auth()` returns, including while `finally` waits for `_lock`. Concurrent `re_auth_callback` therefore stores the new token instead of authenticating, and `release()` then puts the connection in `_available_connections` still using the old credentials.
Additional Locations (1) - [`redis/asyncio/connection.py#L3354-L3368`](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/2b4eaa6928457c22b9d954dd25ba937032f12ecc/redis/asyncio/connection.py#L3354-L3368)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 2b4eaa6928457c22b9d954dd25ba937032f12ecc. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Internal: new commit on fix/async-pool-release-reauth (not pushed). Both findings were real and were introduced by this PR's earlier ordering (not pre-existing: master dispatched after the lock/append and had no gap for the token, nor the foreign-connection side effects). Tests: `test_release__token_queued_while_re_auth_pending__applied` and `test_release__connection_not_in_pool__no_side_effects` both fail on the previous commit (2b4eaa69) and pass now. Pool/credentials/maint/connection suite with redis-server: 351 passed / 14 failed (the usual password/ACL ones, same on master). ruff clean. Design: release() now holds self._lock across remove -> reconnect check -> dispatch -> append, so re_auth_callback() (which needs the lock) can't run in between; it matches BlockingConnectionPool, which already holds its condition across the dispatch. Cost: the pool lock is held for the AUTH round trip, as re_auth_callback() already does for idle connections. The earlier "recheck should_reconnect in the finally" was dropped: update_active_connections_for_reconnect() takes the same lock, so it can't mark a connection mid-release any more.


Good catch, this was real. With the event dispatched before the final lock, a token queued by `re_auth_callback()` while the release waited for the lock stayed queued on a connection that was already available. `release()` now keeps `_lock` from removing the connection from the in-use set until it is added to the available list, listeners included, so `re_auth_callback()` runs either before the release (the token is applied by the deferred `re_auth()`) or after it (the connection is available, so it gets the `AUTH` directly). New test `test_release__token_queued_while_re_auth_pending__applied` fails on the previous commit and passes with e57a4e23.

Also real. `release()` now removes the connection from the in-use set first, so a foreign or already-released connection raises `KeyError` before any reconnect handling or listener runs, as before this PR. New test `test_release__connection_not_in_pool__no_side_effects` covers it; it fails on the previous commit.

Same race as the Codex P1 above, fixed in the same commit: the connection stays under the pool lock until it is available, so a concurrent `re_auth_callback()` can no longer leave its token queued on it.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid re-entering the pool lock from release listeners**

When RESP3 maintenance notifications and streaming credentials are both enabled, the deferred `re_auth()` invoked here can receive a `MOVING` push before the AUTH reply; the parser awaits `AsyncMaintNotificationsPoolHandler.handle_notification()`, which calls `ConnectionPool.apply_moving_notification()` and tries to acquire this same non-reentrant `_lock`. The release task therefore waits on its own lock while holding it, blocking every checkout/release on the pool indefinitely. Keep this connection reserved without awaiting listener/socket work under the pool lock.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L92-L92](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/e57a4e23679ed95d3d30342918efbef368ee2854/AGENTS.md#L92-L92)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep releasing connections visible to pool shutdown**

When pool shutdown overlaps a deferred re-auth, removing the connection here puts it in neither `_in_use_connections` nor `_available_connections` until the listener finishes. `disconnect(inuse_connections=True)`/`aclose()` only iterate those collections, so they return without closing this socket; `release()` then appends a still-connected connection after shutdown, as can happen when another task closes the client during credential rotation. Keep it tracked as in-use until dispatch completes or explicitly coordinate shutdown with this transition.

### Deadlock during deferred re-auth I/O **High Severity** Holding `_lock` across `dispatch_async` runs deferred `re_auth()` socket I/O while the pool lock is still held. A RESP3 `MOVING` push handled in that `read_response` calls `apply_moving_notification`, which acquires the same non-reentrant `asyncio.Lock` on the same task and hangs every checkout and release.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e57a4e23679ed95d3d30342918efbef368ee2854. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Close misses connection during re-auth **Medium Severity** `release()` removes the connection from `_in_use_connections` before listeners run and only appends it to `_available_connections` afterward. `disconnect()` and `aclose()` walk those two lists without the pool lock, so a close that overlaps pending re-auth never sees the live socket and leaves it connected after shutdown.
Additional Locations (1) - [`redis/asyncio/connection.py#L3294-L3312`](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/e57a4e23679ed95d3d30342918efbef368ee2854/redis/asyncio/connection.py#L3294-L3312)

Good catch, you're right: a `MOVING` push read during the AUTH reply goes through `apply_moving_notification`, which takes the same non-reentrant pool lock. `release()` no longer holds the lock while the listeners run (5d4f7c24). The connection stays in the in-use set during the listeners, and the lock is taken only to move it to the available list, and only if `re_auth_callback()` didn't queue a new token in the meantime (otherwise the listeners run again). `test_release__re_auth_needs_the_pool_lock__no_deadlock` hangs on e57a4e23 and passes now.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve newer tokens across in-flight re-auth**

When token A is already queued as release starts and token B arrives while `AbstractConnection.re_auth()` is awaiting A's AUTH reply, this marker records B, but `re_auth()` then unconditionally clears `_re_auth_token` after A's reply (line 1704). The loop observes the marker but its next listener call sees no token, so only A reaches Redis and this connection becomes available under stale credentials after B replaces or outlives A; the sync pool serializes this callback and sends B, so preserve B separately or clear the captured A before awaiting.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Dispatch each connection-release event only once**

When a credential rotation sets `_re_auth_queued` while `dispatch_async()` is awaiting any release listener, the subsequent `continue` re-enters this loop and dispatches another `AsyncAfterConnectionReleasedEvent`. `EventDispatcher.register_listeners()` allows callers to attach arbitrary async listeners, so one logical `release()` now repeats all of their side effects once per overlapping rotation, whereas both the previous async implementation and the sync pool dispatch the release event once; retry only the deferred re-auth operation rather than the whole event.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L146-L148](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/5d4f7c2419e3ae35d5f565cf0ef5617928a01961/AGENTS.md#L146-L148)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

### Queued re-auth token can be dropped **Medium Severity** A token that arrives while deferred AUTH is in flight is stored on the connection and tracked in `_re_auth_queued`, but `re_auth()` then sets `_re_auth_token` to `None` when the in-flight AUTH completes, wiping the replacement. The release loop retries, sees no token, and returns the connection without applying the new credentials. The new test starts with no pending token and stubs `re_auth()` so it does not cover this production path.
Additional Locations (1) - [`redis/asyncio/connection.py#L3393-L3396`](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/5d4f7c2419e3ae35d5f565cf0ef5617928a01961/redis/asyncio/connection.py#L3393-L3396)

@petyaslavova I missed that #4433 by @zhechen-cs, opened on 10-14, fixes the same release/re-auth race in the same files, so this PR duplicates it. Sorry for the overlap. I'm happy to close this one in favour of #4433. In case it's useful there, the review rounds here turned up three cases worth a test: a `MOVING` notification read during the deferred `AUTH` reply needs the pool lock (so the listeners can't run under it), `disconnect()`/`aclose()` must still see a connection whose re-auth is pending, and a token queued by `re_auth_callback()` during a release must still be applied.

Hey @pcbeingused333, thank you for your contribution!

Thanks for flagging the overlap yourself. #4433 fixes the same race in the same place and already has the design from my review there (dispatch outside the pool lock, connection kept in use, and `re_auth()` clearing only the token it sent), so I'm going to close this one as a duplicate. The cases you listed are useful: the listener-takes-the-pool-lock test is covered there, and keeping the connection in the in-use set during the dispatch keeps it visible to `disconnect()`/`aclose()`.
